text: Can you describe how long these episodes of unresponsiveness typically last, and do you have any memory of the events afterward? I also need to know if there is a specific trigger, such as flashing lights or stress, that precedes these episodes.

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of head trauma, fever, or previous seizures, and does your family have any history of epilepsy? I also need to know if these episodes occur primarily during sleep or while he is awake and active.

speaker: Doctor
text: No history of head trauma, fever, or previous seizures. Family history is negative for epilepsy. The episodes occur both during the day and night, but seem more frequent in the evening.
